newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX declines in technical correction.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX declines in technical correction.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange gave up half percent on Wednesday, although just before the close of play the BUX index went into positive territory, in what dealers said was a technical correction.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 7,373.08 points, down 39.63 points or 0.53 percent.

"There was a technical correction, which is natural after such a big rise, but the underlying trend has not changed," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities. He referred to an almost two percent rally on Tuesday to a new closing high.
Traders were confident about the market's short-term outlook, saying investors began to buy at lower price levels.
Market participants said fresh capital was continuously seeking investment opportunities in Hungary, with an increasing eagerness by local investors.
"Today foreign investors were on the selling side in early trade and domestic buyers were able to hold the market," Forgo said.
Gabor Sitanyi, analyst at ING Barings in London, said that a downward correction was unlikely to come as unexpected factors were working in favour of the Hungarian market.
"The floods came unexpectedly and meant that neither the Polish nor the Czech markets are very exciting at the moment," Sitanyi said.
He added that as a result of trade and current account deficit fears in Poland, Russia and Hungary remained the key investment targets in the eastern European region, at least for a while.
"Of course, new and exciting markets are joining, with Romania gearing up, while investment rules in Slovenia were changed," Sitanyi said, adding that the Ukraine would follow.
Others traders said earlier today that expectations of good first half corporate earnings and hopes for early EU membership talks will start to be factored in prices.
On Wednesday BUX futures also reflected optimism, Forgo said, adding futures ended higher for all maturities but September which eased 9.5 points to finish at 7,650 points.
"Futures markets reflect optimism as they strengthened despite the correction on the spot market," Forgo said, adding that yield contents rose.
On Wednesday, retailer Fotex closed more than 10 percent firmer at 245 forints.
Curtain manufacturer Gardenia firmed 85 forints or 4.51 percent to finish at 1,970 forints, and a trader said the move reflected the fact that the share was undervalued.
Gas distributor Primagaz ended at 10,345 forints, up 20, after a "buy" recommendation by Hungarian securities house New York Broker Budapest in a technical research.
Elsewhere, OTP Bank rallied to a new high of 6,450 forints, before an agency cross in the last deal of the day beat it down to close at 6,250 forints, down 40.
